title: Ecclesiastes 7
paragraphs: ¹ A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death better than the day of birth. ² It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for death is the destiny of everyone; the living should take this to heart. ³ Frustration is better than laughter, because a sad face is good for the heart. ⁴ The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure. ⁵ It is better to heed the rebuke of a wise person than to listen to the song of fools.

⁶ Like the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless. ⁷ Extortion turns a wise person into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart. ⁸ The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience is better than pride. ⁹ Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger lives in the lap of fools. ¹⁰ Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" It is not wisdom to ask such things.

¹¹ Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing and benefits those who see the sun. ¹² Wisdom is a shelter, just as money is a shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom preserves those who have it. ¹³ Consider what God has done: who can straighten what he has made crooked? ¹⁴ When times are good, be happy; when times are bad, consider this: God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore no one can discover anything about their future. ¹⁵ In my meaningless life I have seen both of these: the righteous perishing in their righteousness, and the wicked living long in their wickedness.

¹⁶ Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise — why should you destroy yourself? ¹⁷ Do not be overly wicked, and do not be a fool — why should you die before your time? ¹⁸ It is good to grasp the one and not let go of the other. The person who fears God will avoid all extremes. ¹⁹ Wisdom makes one wise person more powerful than ten rulers in a city. ²⁰ Indeed, there is no one on earth who is righteous — no one who does what is right and never sins.

²¹ Do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you — ²² for you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others. ²³ All this I tested by wisdom. I said, "I am determined to be wise" — but wisdom was beyond my reach. ²⁴ What exists is far off and unfathomably deep. Who can discover it? ²⁵ So I turned my attention to understanding and to search out and seek wisdom and the explanation of things, and to understand the foolishness of wickedness and the madness of folly.

²⁶ I find something more bitter than death: the kind of woman who is a trap — her heart a snare, her hands like chains. The one who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will be caught. ²⁷ "Look," says the Teacher, "this is what I found when I added one thing to another to reach a conclusion — ²⁸ which I am still searching for but have not found: I found one upright man among a thousand, but not one upright woman among them all." ²⁹ This only have I found: God made humanity upright, but they have gone in search of many schemes.
